The study unifies these diverse behaviors under a single percolation paradigm, suggesting that vibrational spectroscopies offer unique, non-destructive insight into the mesoscopic organization of alloys, a scale previously inaccessible by macroscopic approximations. summary.title: Uniﬁcation of the phonon mode behaviour in semiconductor alloys
summary.authors: O. Pag`es, M. Kassem, A. Chaﬁ, A. Nassour, S. Doyen and A. V. Postnikov
summary.executive_summary: This study challenges the traditional classification of phonon mode behavior in semiconductor alloys, which relies on the Virtual Crystal Approximation (VCA) and Coherent Potential Approximation (CPA). The authors investigate three representative systems: In1−xGaxAs, In1−xGaxP, and ZnTe1−xSex. While the first two were previously understood as 1-bond→1-mode or modified 2-mode systems under VCA, this work demonstrates that ZnTe1−xSex actually exhibits a 1-bond→2-mode behavior, identical to the others. By analyzing Transverse Optical (TO) phonon frequencies via Raman and Infrared spectroscopy, the authors propose a universal 'percolation' model. This model describes the alloy disorder at a mesoscopic scale, where local bond distortions create distinct B-rich and C-rich regions. The study unifies these diverse behaviors under a single percolation paradigm, suggesting that vibrational spectroscopies offer unique, non-destructive insight into the mesoscopic organization of alloys, a scale previously inaccessible by macroscopic approximations. The findings refute the sufficiency of VCA for describing bond force constants in these mixtures and highlight the critical role of local topology over macroscopic averaging.
